The role leads the management of all awards and partnerships within the Country Office, ensuring robust systems, processes, and controls are in place to support effective programme delivery, donor compliance, portfolio performance, and risk management. The Head of Awards, Localisation and Partnerships will establish and promote best-practice award management processes, working closely with the Programme Development and Quality (PDQ), Finance, Operations, and Programme teams to ensure the successful implementation and oversight of awards. In addition, the role provides strategic leadership on localisation and partnership development, strengthening engagement with local actors and ensuring the Country Office's localisation commitments are embedded throughout programme design, implementation, and partnership management. The post holder will serve as the focal point for members and donors on award-related matters, fostering strong relationships and ensuring responsive, solution-oriented communication. The Head of Awards, Localisation and Partnerships is accountable for the performance of the award portfolio, monitoring risks and opportunities, driving timely corrective actions, and ensuring award management systems and processes are consistently applied across all departments. Through effective leadership, coordination, and stakeholder engagement, the role contributes to the achievement of programme objectives, sustainable partnerships, donor confidence, and the overall strategic growth of the Kenya Country Office. Scope Of Role Reports to: Country Director Staff reporting to this post: 4 staff - Awards and Partership Coordinator, Awards and Finance Officer, Awards and Partnership Assistant and Awards and Partnership Intern.. Budget Responsibilities : None Role Dimensions : The Head of Awards, Localisation and Partnerships is responsible for managing a portfolio of high-, medium-, and low-risk awards within the Kenya Country Office, providing strong leadership and oversight, particularly for high-risk and complex awards. The role requires extensive internal and external coordination, stakeholder engagement, and strategic support across all aspects of award management, including award contracting, donor compliance, reporting, and portfolio performance management. The post holder is accountable for ensuring compliance with Save the Children's Award Management Essential Standards and Award Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) across the Kenya portfolio. Acting as the central coordination point between PDQ, Finance, and Operations, the Awards Manager ensures effective award management throughout the entire award lifecycle. The role serves as the primary focal point for Members and donors, maintaining responsive, solution-oriented communication and fostering strong working relationships. The Head of Awards, Localisation and Partnerships leads the partnership portfolio and locally led delivery modality, ensuring high-quality programs are delivered at scale through strategic and equitable partnerships. The role drives the operationalization of the localisation strategy across its seven dimensions and embeds partners throughout the full programme cycle, from design to implementation and learning, while strengthening systems, processes, and risk-sharing practices. The role is responsible for monitoring award performance, proactively identifying and escalating risks and issues, and ensuring timely implementation of mitigation measures. The position also ensures that award management systems, processes, and controls are effectively implemented and adhered to across all departments, with a particular focus on donor compliance, reporting quality, financial stewardship, and timely delivery of award obligations. Through strong coordination and leadership, the role contributes to maximizing funding opportunities, reducing compliance risks, and enhancing the overall effectiveness and efficiency of the Country Office portfolio. Travel: Occasional Key Areas Of Accountability Portfolio Planning, Development, and Management: Coordinate the submission of all required information and documentation into AMS by relevant functions in a timely manner as new funding opportunities are identified. Review award agreements to identify potential risks and provide summaries of key risk areas. Participate in go/no-go decision-making processes with Members and the Senior Management Team (SMT), including opportunity and risk assessments. Develop funding optimization strategies in collaboration with the Finance team, including match plans, CAM, and other funding mechanisms. Support the Country Director (CD) and SPD Manager in strengthening engagement and relationship management with Members and donor representatives on award management and compliance matters. In collaboration with the PDQ team, provide strategic portfolio information to the SMT and Save the Children Members through a monthly portfolio analysis report, highlighting pipeline opportunities, active awards, awards under amendment, high-risk awards, and closed awards. Award Management And AMS Management Ensure all award lifecycle processes are completed through AMS workflows in a timely manner and that all relevant information is accurately maintained within the system and in hard-copy files where required. Liaise directly with Members to ensure timely issuance of workflows and fund summaries following award approval. Establish mechanisms for disseminating award information to ensure all key staff understand award requirements and expectations throughout the award lifecycle. Ensure kick-off meetings are conducted promptly for all new awards and that coding structures and budgets are effectively communicated to budget holders. Lead Member engagement and relationship management as the SCI focal point for awards, coordinating SCI/Member reviews and revisions of proposals, budgets, and agreements. Provide regular updates to the Finance Manager on new awards that impact Master Budget gap analysis and co-lead the maintenance of the CAM calculator. Lead the analysis of Budget versus Actual Expenditure (BVA) reports for monthly award review meetings. Work with budget holders to develop and implement corrective action plans and monitor progress against agreed actions. Coordinate monthly award review meetings and maintain a tracker of action points and outstanding issues. Provide guidance on budget coding and reallocations in collaboration with budget holders. Coordinate budget realignments, amendments, cost extensions, and no-cost extension requests to Members and donors in a timely manner. Work closely with Programme Operations to ensure timely award close-out meetings. Ensure all meetings are documented, minutes are filed in AMS, and follow-up actions are completed. Ensure AMS is accurately maintained, up to date, and provides a complete audit trail for all awards and sub-awards. Support Programme Managers in budget development, cost allocation, budget monitoring, phasing, and forecasting, ensuring that phased award budgets are uploaded into Agresso. Reporting To Members And Donors Coordinate the award reporting process to ensure high-quality reports are submitted within agreed timelines. Share the award reporting schedule with the Extended Senior Management Team on the first working day of each month. Support the preparation of financial reports, with responsibility transitioning to Finance once appropriate staffing capacity is established. Review all award reports prior to submission to Members and donors to ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance. Share Members' qualitative feedback on reports with relevant stakeholders on a monthly basis. Ensure donors and Members are informed of any significant award-related issues. Manage contractual relationships with donors and Members through effective communication on reports, contracts, amendments, and audits. Collaborate with relevant functions and Members to strengthen project staff capacity in quality reporting. Donor Compliance Ensure donor compliance requirements, including reporting deadlines, amendment procedures, audit requirements, and SCI award management policies, are clearly understood and adhered to. Ensure potential compliance issues and amendment requests are promptly communicated to donors through the relevant Save the Children Member. Develop business cases and support negotiations where donor waivers or derogation requests require detailed justification. Collaborate with Member focal points to ensure all donor compliance requirements are captured in AMS before fund summary workflows are initiated. Localisation Lead the implementation of the Country Office Localization Strategy, in line with Save the Children’s Global Partnership Framework, Localization Policy, Grand Bargain commitments, and CHS standards. Ensure partnership and localization priorities are fully integrated into country strategic planning, annual plans, and humanitarian response strategies. Drive the operationalization of localization across its seven dimensions, identifying and addressing operational bottlenecks and influencing systems, processes, and decision-making. Coordinate periodic self-assessments on partnerships and localization, ensuring action plans are developed, implemented, monitored, and reported to SMT Partnership Management Provide capacity-building and compliance support to both new and existing partners, working closely with Programme Operations to ensure partner performance meets donor expectations. Conduct regular spot checks to ensure all partner documentation, including reports, is uploaded and maintained within AMS. Lead and coordinate partner scoping, mapping, assessment, and selection processes in collaboration with PDQI and program teams. ( implementing the Equitable Partnership Management Cycle) Ensure partners are actively engaged in programme design, proposal development, planning, and budgeting, including adequate resourcing of partner support and capacity strengthening. Staff Management And Development Strengthen the capacity of the Award Management Team in award lifecycle management and build the capacity of budget holders on their award management roles and responsibilities. Manage the performance of direct reports through effective application of SCI's Performance Management System. Address underperformance through clear documentation, performance improvement plans, and structured development work plans. Foster a culture of accountability, continuous learning, and professional development within the team. BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice ) Accountability holds self accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities - giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved. Ambition sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages their team to do the same widely shares their personal vision for Save the Children, engages and motivates others future orientated, thinks strategically and on a global scale. Collaboration builds and maintains effective relationships, with their team, colleagues, Members and external partners and supporters values diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength approachable, good listener, easy to talk to Creativity develops and encourages new and innovative solutions willing to take disciplined risks. Integrity honest, encourages openness and transparency; demonstrates highest levels of integrity Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in International Development, Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a related field. Professional accounting qualification (CPA, ACCA, or equivalent) is highly desirable. Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in award, grant, portfolio, or financial management, preferably within an international NGO or donor-funded environment, including at least 7 years in a senior leadership role. Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-donor portfolios and leading cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality programme and award management outcomes. Essential EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS Proven experience in staff management, supervision, coaching, and capacity building, particularly in award and grant management. Significant experience managing complex award portfolios and donor-funded programmes. Proven track record in grant and contract management, including sub-award administration and donor compliance. Strong knowledge of major institutional donor requirements and regulations, including but not limited to USAID, FCDO, ECHO, EU, UNICEF, WFP, and other bilateral and multilateral donors. review_candidates.title: HR Director, Asia Pacific
review_candidates.description: Who We Are International Justice Mission (IJM) is the global leader in protecting vulnerable people from violence around the world. Our team of over 1,200 professionals are at work worldwide in over 30 offices. Together we are on a mission to rescue millions, protect half a billion, and make justice unstoppable. We are a global community that cares for one another. We believe that the way we work is as important as the results we achieve. We provide professional excellence with joy and celebration to all those we serve. The Need For over 25 years, IJM has pioneered the work to protect vulnerable people from violence. 9 out of 9 times in the last decade, IJM’s Justice System Strengthening Projects have reduced slavery and violence between 50 and 85% for very large populations of people in poverty. As we grow to expand our impact to protect 500 million people from violence, we are seeking an HR Director, Asia Pacific to enhance organizational effectiveness by partnering closely with regional and global leaders to align HR strategies with IJM's mission and priorities. The HR Director plays a strategic and innovative role supporting business growth, talent acquisition and development in complex, matrixed environments, while embedding a culture of agility, data-driven decision-making, and strategic partnership. The position collaborates closely with regional leadership, including the Regional President, Regional Vice Presidents, Regional General Counsel, Country Directors, management teams, and Global People Support (GPS) to ensure adherence to global standards while appropriately adapting to local labor laws, cultural contexts, and emerging business needs. The Asia Pacific Region includes Program Offices and Advancement Offices across ten countries with approximately 265 staff members. This role sits within the Regional Operations and Integration team and partners with colleagues supporting program, operations, and resourcing objectives throughout the region. This hybrid position may be based in Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, or Thailand; reports to the Vice President, Operations & Integration, Asia Pacific; and is only available to candidates with current work authorization in the country in which they will be employed. Responsibilities: Strategy & Knowledge Development & Implementation Actively participate in regional leadership team strategic planning, contributing HR insights that drive organizational objectives; Develop and monitor regional HR policies, ensuring compliance with enterprise standards and labor laws through regular auditing and timely corrective actions; Lead regional implementation of global HR systems, tools and processes (salary annual reviews, annual performance reviews, employee engagement, etc.) in support of APAC leadership; Develop and maintain partnerships with external HR vendors and service providers to support regional HR operations; and Mentor and coach regional and country HR leaders and teams to enhance HR capacity and effectiveness. Policies and Procedures Proactively review and recommend improvements to HR policies, procedures, compensation, benefits, and practices to enhance compliance, contextualization; socialization and awareness, engagement, and alignment with global standards. Collaborate with GPS to align regional HR best practices within the global framework; and Apply deep knowledge of regional employment law and risk management. Communication and Employee Relations Provide expert guidance on complex regional employee relations issues, equipping managers to navigate sensitive matters successfully; Ensure that communications and change management initiatives maintain a people-centric focus, effectively supporting the needs of leadership and teams; Lead compliant employee relations practices through transparent and fair policies, processes and procedures that mitigate risk and enhance employee experience and trust; and Have a deep understanding of disciplinary, capability, misconduct, investigation policies, procedures and lead teams in fair and effective delivery. Recruitment and Rewards Lead the HR team to deliver the talent pipeline in collaboration with country leaders and aligned to the regional budget, recruitment and equal opportunity policies and engagement with technical platform solutions e.g. Workday recruitment module ATS; Champion safe recruitment practices that mitigate risk to the organization and its stakeholders and ensure background checks are legal and complete; Understand deeply and lead on the hiring and contracting models relevant to the region including local and expatriate employment, employers of record, procurement of consultants and partner with legal to ensure compliance with legal; Ensure the program countries in region align to the global pay and global mobility policies, job evaluation frameworks and job titling conventions to ensure internal standardization and pay equity; Act as HR partner to global functions hiring in region to ensure hosted employment in region is understood by all stakeholders and managed well for the best employee experience; Lead the annual pay review process ensuring that the country leaders and HR receive the training and support they need; and Lead and deliver the recruitment, contracting, payroll and rewards for the regional support team. Training and Development Lead the regional performance management process, ensuring timely communication and training for managers and staff; Lead regional employee engagement aligned with the global process and hold ownership and accountability for monitoring regional action plans; Identify and recommend relevant training and development opportunities supporting employee growth and organizational needs; Monitor, assess, and report on workforce retention, promotion, and succession planning efforts in partnership with GPS; Plan resource needs and assist in developing recruitment and onboarding programs aligned with IJM values and global strategies; identify and address retention risks; and Lead the region to comply with technical platform solutions e.g. LMS Documentation, Reporting & Data Management Develop and present regional People KPIs to leadership, leveraging data analytics to drive informed HR and business decisions; Analyze workforce metrics to support talent strategy design and communicate findings effectively to key stakeholders; and Collaborate with finance and legal teams to develop and monitor HR budgets and compliance adherence. Compliance Ensure employment statutory compliance in each country in their Region; Collaborate with budget managers on HR-related budget planning and expense monitoring; Collaborate closely with GPS to maintain excellence in HR service delivery; and Manage employee separation processes including exit packages, interviews and asset recovery. Networking & Partnership Build and sustain strategic HR partnerships with regional leadership, line managers, and cross-functional teams; Champion spiritual formation initiatives and nurture an inclusive and motivating work environment aligned with IJM’s values; and Regularly engage with employees, country leadership, interns, and fellows to encourage their development, well-being, and engagement. General Tasks Engage fully in IJM’s community of spiritual formation, upholding organizational values in all professional activities and behaviors. Qualifications: Master's qualification in a relevant field, SHRM-SCP, GPHR, or equivalent HR certification recognized across Asia Pacific; Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible Human Resources experience, ideally within complex, matrixed, and global organizations; Experience within INGOs preferred but not required; Demonstrated experience with HR systems such as Workday; Experience in business operations, financial literacy, budgeting, and data-driven HR management; Experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from strategy through execution; Experience training and developing managers in performance management, employee relations, and employee engagement practices; Experience leading talent acquisition, compensation, and rewards programs aligned with organizational strategy; Proven success partnering with senior leaders and executives; Experience working across culturally diverse and geographically dispersed teams; Experience in line management and people leadership; Strong knowledge of employment law and labor practices across multiple Asia Pacific jurisdictions; Experience with expatriate and local employment models, including visa and work permit considerations; Proficiency in English required, with additional regional language skills considered an advantage; and Existing authorization to work in one of the identified hiring locations without sponsorship. Critical Qualities: Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, and operational execution capabilities; Excellent interpersonal, training, coaching, and stakeholder engagement skills; Highly collaborative approach and solution-oriented mindset; Proficiency in HR analytics and evidence-based decision-making; Strong policy development, implementation, compliance, and risk management capabilities; Ability to navigate ambiguity and lead organizational change with resilience and creativity; Strong business acumen and understanding of organizational financials; Self-awareness, curiosity, agility, empathy, and commitment to continuous growth; Ability to build credibility and trust across diverse stakeholder groups; and Willingness and ability to travel within the region and internationally as needed. Application Process: Upload Resume & Cover Letter in one PDF document. IJM holds strict safeguarding principles and a zero tolerance to violations of the Safeguarding Policy, Protection against Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment Policy, and Code of Ethics. Candidate selection is based on technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring criteria subject to assessing the candidate’s value congruence and thorough background, police clearance, and reference check processes. IJM requires a background check, police clearance and thorough review of references with an employment offer and/or employment contract.
